newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ money market takes heart at close from TWI.
newsitem.headline: NZ money market takes heart at close from TWI.

* NZ bills end a touch stronger as TWI climbs
* Bid tone in bonds after eurokiwi, U.S. strength
* Volumes reasonable
New Zealand's money market closed with a bid tone on Wednesday, taking heart from the continued strength of the currency's Trade-Weighted Index.
The 90-day bank bills ended a couple of basis points stronger at 7.36 percent while the TWI rose to 68.50 from its 68.23 finish on Tuesday.
One dealer said if the TWI could manage an average of 68.10 next week the bills would be comfortable pushing down to 7.25 percent.

"The currency has obviously been short-squeezed all the way up...and the 0.6925 level is providing a bit of resistance, so we may see the TWI come back down a little bit overnight, to the 68.30 level or somewhere around there," he added.

Bonds ended steady to slightly stronger after an early boost from a NZ$100 million March 1999 bond issued overnight on behalf of Commerzbank. Continued strength in U.S. Treasuries was also encouraging buying in the local market and volumes were fairly good, dealers said.
The U.S. is expected to take centre-stage in the short term, with the conclusion of a Federal Reserve meeting, followed by non-farm payrolls data out on Friday.
Meanwhile, Bankers Trust New Zealand said in a statement that recent house price data and credit aggregate data were not encouraging for New Zealand's inflation outlook.
Reserve Bank of New Zealand data released on Wednesday showed private sector credit (the revised series) up 1.9 percent in the December month, following a 0.2 percent fall in November.
Preliminary Valuation New Zealand figures on Tuesday showed house price figures rising 2.5 percent in the December quarter.

BTNZ said it was disturbing that the rises occurred when there was considerable political uncertainty, and before the full effect of the significant fall in wholesale interest rates flowed through into retail interest rates.
